name: Winter Home Maintenance Checklist
description: A winter home maintenance checklist for cold-weather upkeep and protecting your home.

items.text: Insulate exposed pipes in the garage, crawl space and exterior walls
Let faucets drip slowly during hard freezes
items.note: Moving water is far less likely to freeze

items.text: Keep the thermostat at 55°F or higher, even when away
Open cabinet doors to let warm air reach pipes under sinks
Know where the main water shut-off is in case a pipe bursts
Keep the garage door closed to protect any plumbing inside
Replace furnace filters monthly during heavy heating use
Keep supply and return vents clear of furniture and rugs
Listen for unusual furnace noises and call a pro if heat fails
Use space heaters safely — on hard floors, away from fabric, never unattended
Run a humidifier to offset dry winter air and protect woodwork
Have a backup heat source and fuel ready for power outages
Watch for icicles and ice buildup at the roof edge
Rake light roof snow from the ground with a roof rake
Check the attic for adequate insulation and ventilation
items.note: Warm attics melt snow and cause ice dams

items.text: Keep gutters and downspouts clear so meltwater can drain
Hire a professional for heavy roof snow or steep roofs
Test smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms on every level
Check CO alarms near the furnace, fireplace and attached garage
items.note: CO is odorless; alarms are the only reliable warning

items.text: Keep the fireplace flue clear and never burn trash or treated wood
Keep the kitchen fire extinguisher accessible and charged
Avoid running generators or grills indoors or in the garage
Add or replace weatherstripping on drafty doors and windows
Use draft stoppers under exterior doors
Apply window insulation film to single-pane windows
Lock windows fully to seal the gap and improve security
Keep curtains open on sunny days and closed at night for warmth
Keep walkways, steps and the driveway clear of snow and ice
Stock ice melt and a working snow shovel near the door
Confirm outdoor faucets are drained and shut off
Stock an emergency kit: flashlight, batteries, water and blankets
Trim or note branches weighed down by ice that could fall

faq.q: How do I keep pipes from freezing in winter?
faq.a: Insulate exposed pipes, let faucets drip during hard freezes, keep the heat above 55°F even when away, and open cabinet doors so warm air reaches plumbing along exterior walls.

faq.q: Can I download this winter checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print this winter home maintenance checklist or download it as a PDF and keep it handy to run the quick checks before each cold snap.

faq.q: What is an ice dam and how do I prevent it?
faq.a: An ice dam is a ridge of ice at the roof edge that traps melting snow and forces water under shingles. Good attic insulation and ventilation, plus clearing roof snow safely, help prevent them.

faq.q: Why is carbon monoxide a bigger risk in winter?
faq.a: Closed windows and heavy use of furnaces, fireplaces and space heaters raise the chance of carbon-monoxide buildup. Working CO alarms on every level are essential through the heating season.

faq.q: Should I remove snow from my roof myself?
faq.a: Use a long-handled roof rake from the ground for light buildup. For heavy snow or steep roofs, hire a professional — climbing onto an icy roof is dangerous and can cause damage.
